blocks.text: Dohra:
It was in the year eignteen hundred and eight, The year of great massacre (Ghallughara) it was. After ransacking the Brars (of the Malwa region), That the United Khalsa Panth force made a move. (1)
lines: It was in the year eignteen hundred and eight,
The year of great massacre (Ghallughara) it was.
After ransacking the Brars (of the Malwa region),
That the United Khalsa Panth force made a move.

blocks.text: Chopai:

Thereafter did Ala Singh approach the Khalsa Singhs, With him did he bring his Phulkian fraternity. With him did he bring Singhs from Bhai dynasty, Who were led by Bhai Buddha Singh and Gurbakhsh Singh. (2)
lines: Thereafter did Ala Singh approach the Khalsa Singhs,
With him did he bring his Phulkian fraternity.
With him did he bring Singhs from Bhai dynasty,
Who were led by Bhai Buddha Singh and Gurbakhsh Singh.

blocks.text: For attacking the Malerkotla rulers did he suggest, As there existed an enmity between Pathans and Malwais. So after looting, plundering and taking over their territory, The Khalsa Panth force marched ahead of Malerkotla. (3)
lines: For attacking the Malerkotla rulers did he suggest,
As there existed an enmity between Pathans and Malwais.
So after looting, plundering and taking over their territory,
The Khalsa Panth force marched ahead of Malerkotla.

blocks.text: As the Khalsa Panth force moved towards Sirhind, They returned as they saw the orchards around the city. The Mughal force which was stationed inside the city, It failed to come out being scared of the Khalsa force. (4)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth force moved towards Sirhind,
They returned as they saw the orchards around the city.
The Mughal force which was stationed inside the city,
It failed to come out being scared of the Khalsa force.

blocks.text: As the Khalsa found the Mughals morale quite low, The Khalsa felt emboldened at their own military strength. Reckoning the Mughals as timid as a frightened rabbit, They could capture and kill the Sirhind Mughals later on. (5)
lines: As the Khalsa found the Mughals morale quite low,
The Khalsa felt emboldened at their own military strength.
Reckoning the Mughals as timid as a frightened rabbit,
They could capture and kill the Sirhind Mughals later on.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Khalsa called an assembly of local inhabitants of the area, Who resided in and around the city of Sirhind. They must shortlist ten enemies of the Khalsa Panth, Who must be eliminated with the guidance of the locals. (6)
lines: The Khalsa called an assembly of local inhabitants of the area,
Who resided in and around the city of Sirhind.
They must shortlist ten enemies of the Khalsa Panth,
Who must be eliminated with the guidance of the locals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

There were Singhs in the Khalsa force from villages Gharuan1 and Salodi2 , Who had been with the Khalsa Panth since the beginning. Both these Khalsa Singhs pointed out with one voice, That the Muslims of Morinda were the worst enemies of the Singhs. (7)
lines: There were Singhs in the Khalsa force from villages Gharuan1 and Salodi2 ,
Who had been with the Khalsa Panth since the beginning.
Both these Khalsa Singhs pointed out with one voice,
That the Muslims of Morinda were the worst enemies of the Singhs.

blocks.text: Their Muslim rulers were instrumental in the arrest of Sahibzadas, Thereafter had Wazir Khan slaughtered the Guru's sons. Both these Singhs suggested to the Khalsa Panth force, Must the Khalsa not spare those enemies at any cost. (8)
lines: Their Muslim rulers were instrumental in the arrest of Sahibzadas,
Thereafter had Wazir Khan slaughtered the Guru's sons.
Both these Singhs suggested to the Khalsa Panth force,
Must the Khalsa not spare those enemies at any cost.

blocks.text: S. Jassa Singh Ahluwalia wished to put it off for the time being, As he apprehended Abdali's troops in the near vicinity. In case the Khalsa failed to capture Morinda till evening, Abdali's Pathan troops might return to join the Morinda Muslims. (9)
lines: S.
Jassa Singh Ahluwalia wished to put it off for the time being,
As he apprehended Abdali's troops in the near vicinity.
In case the Khalsa failed to capture Morinda till evening,
Abdali's Pathan troops might return to join the Morinda Muslims.

blocks.text: As the moment of Morinda rulers' death had approached, Who could put off what was ordained by the Divine Will? As whatever was destined had to happen at all, The Khalsa Panth force coincidently moved towards Morinda. (10)
lines: As the moment of Morinda rulers' death had approached,
Who could put off what was ordained by the Divine Will?
As whatever was destined had to happen at all,
The Khalsa Panth force coincidently moved towards Morinda.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As what is fated has to happen at any cost, Somehow or the other such an occurence does take place. As the movement of truth had arrived at last, The Muslim converts were bound to meet their fated end. (11)
lines: As what is fated has to happen at any cost,
Somehow or the other such an occurence does take place.
As the movement of truth had arrived at last,
The Muslim converts were bound to meet their fated end.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Silently did the Khalsa force march in the same direction, As they had no mind to get into any skirmish (at Morinda). Though the Singhs from Gharuan reminded them again, Nobody paid any heed to these Singhs' entreaties. (12)
lines: Silently did the Khalsa force march in the same direction,
As they had no mind to get into any skirmish (at Morinda).
Though the Singhs from Gharuan reminded them again,
Nobody paid any heed to these Singhs' entreaties.

blocks.text: As the main body of the force had crossed (Morinda), The rear guard of the force was yet to cross the place. As the Divine Will had ordained it to happen here, How could the Divinely ordained occurance be put of? (13)
lines: As the main body of the force had crossed (Morinda),
The rear guard of the force was yet to cross the place.
As the Divine Will had ordained it to happen here,
How could the Divinely ordained occurance be put of?

blocks.text: Whenever the Divine Will wishes an incident to happen, It takes an instant for such an occurance to materialize. A few Singhs of this contingent being thirsty for water, They went to the village (Morinda) to quench their thirst. (14)
lines: Whenever the Divine Will wishes an incident to happen,
It takes an instant for such an occurance to materialize.
A few Singhs of this contingent being thirsty for water,
They went to the village (Morinda) to quench their thirst.

blocks.text: As Tara Singh sent the water-carrier to fetch water, He proceeded and downed his bucket in the well. Ran Singh and Daya Sngh belonging to village Gharuan, They also accompanied the water-carrier to the well. (15)
lines: As Tara Singh sent the water-carrier to fetch water,
He proceeded and downed his bucket in the well.
Ran Singh and Daya Sngh belonging to village Gharuan,
They also accompanied the water-carrier to the well.

blocks.text: Dohra:
There were standing a few Muslim converts (Ranghars), Who were standing atop the rooftops with weapons. As they were abusing the Singhs so loudly, Nobody prohibited them from abusing the Singhs. (16)
lines: There were standing a few Muslim converts (Ranghars),
Who were standing atop the rooftops with weapons.
As they were abusing the Singhs so loudly,
Nobody prohibited them from abusing the Singhs.

blocks.text: As they were indulging in the most vituperative abuses, They called bad names even to the revered Sikh Gurus. Brandishing a blackish rope made of leather, Thse convert (Ranghars) were (denigrating sacred Sikh hair). (17)
lines: As they were indulging in the most vituperative abuses,
They called bad names even to the revered Sikh Gurus.
Brandishing a blackish rope made of leather,
Thse convert (Ranghars) were (denigrating sacred Sikh hair).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Telling the Singhs that black rope was made of Sahibzada's hair, They insinuated the Singhs that the rope had become old and worn. Taunting the Singhs to handover a few more Sikh children, They challenged the Singhs to stand and fight with them. (18)
lines: Telling the Singhs that black rope was made of Sahibzada's hair,
They insinuated the Singhs that the rope had become old and worn.
Taunting the Singhs to handover a few more Sikh children,
They challenged the Singhs to stand and fight with them.

blocks.text: Curse be upon the Singhs if they failed to fight, said they, Why should the Singhs turn their back from the challenge. As they boasted of having slaughtered the Sikh Gurus' sons, They were desperate to eliminate the Guru's Singhs' as well. (19)
lines: Curse be upon the Singhs if they failed to fight, said they,
Why should the Singhs turn their back from the challenge.
As they boasted of having slaughtered the Sikh Gurus' sons,
They were desperate to eliminate the Guru's Singhs' as well.

blocks.text: The Singhs being from the Jat stock and Ranghars from the Rajputs, There had never been a harmony between the two races. As the Singhs belonging to Gharuan heard these abuses, They, too, indulged in hurling abuses at the Ranghars. (20)
lines: The Singhs being from the Jat stock and Ranghars from the Rajputs,
There had never been a harmony between the two races.
As the Singhs belonging to Gharuan heard these abuses,
They, too, indulged in hurling abuses at the Ranghars.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Ranghars heard these counter abuses, They opened a volley of fire at the abusing Singhs. As one of these shots hit one of the Singhs, Who belonged to the contingent of Tara Singh's3 contingent. (21)
lines: As the Ranghars heard these counter abuses,
They opened a volley of fire at the abusing Singhs.
As one of these shots hit one of the Singhs,
Who belonged to the contingent of Tara Singh's3 contingent.

blocks.text: As this bullet shot inflamed Tara Singh (the Misl chief), The divinely ordained moment of truth had arrived. As the Singhs from Gharuan narrated the whole incident, The verbal dual and bullet shot had conflagrated it very much. (22)
lines: As this bullet shot inflamed Tara Singh (the Misl chief),
The divinely ordained moment of truth had arrived.
As the Singhs from Gharuan narrated the whole incident,
The verbal dual and bullet shot had conflagrated it very much.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Gharuan Singhs narrated all the abuses, Which the Ranghars had shouted brandishing a black rope. As these Singhs repeated the abuses hurled at Guru's sons, This narration added more fuel to the burning fire. (23)
lines: The Gharuan Singhs narrated all the abuses,
Which the Ranghars had shouted brandishing a black rope.
As these Singhs repeated the abuses hurled at Guru's sons,
This narration added more fuel to the burning fire.

blocks.text: As all the Singhs flared up upon hearing these words, The situation became very provocative and explosive. S. Tara Singh feeling so much outraged at this, That he ordered the war drum to be beaten. (24)
lines: As all the Singhs flared up upon hearing these words,
The situation became very provocative and explosive.
S.
Tara Singh feeling so much outraged at this,
That he ordered the war drum to be beaten.

blocks.text: As the Singhs shouted the war slogans of Akal! Akal!, His contingent beat the wardrum and unfurled their flag. The Gharuan Singhs finding it the most opportune moment, They raised a lot of hue and cry (for a confrontation) (25)
lines: As the Singhs shouted the war slogans of Akal!
Akal!,
His contingent beat the wardrum and unfurled their flag.
The Gharuan Singhs finding it the most opportune moment,
They raised a lot of hue and cry (for a confrontation)

blocks.text: Messengers were sent posthaste to S. Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Asking him to stop and not to proceed further. Gharuan Singhs themselves ran to catch up with S. Charat Singh, Impressing upon him to attack Morinda without any delay. (26)
lines: Messengers were sent posthaste to S.
Jassa Singh Ahluwalia,
Asking him to stop and not to proceed further.
Gharuan Singhs themselves ran to catch up with S.
Charat Singh,
Impressing upon him to attack Morinda without any delay.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Approaching S. Sham Singh, another Misl chief, They persuaded S. Karora Singh to launch an attack. Thus narrating the whole incident of Ranghar's insolence, They succeeded in getting the attack launched on Morinda. (27)
lines: Approaching S.
Sham Singh, another Misl chief,
They persuaded S.
Karora Singh to launch an attack.
Thus narrating the whole incident of Ranghar's insolence,
They succeeded in getting the attack launched on Morinda.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As S. Hari Singh Bhangi returned with his contingent, So did S. Hari Singh, the chief of the Nankai Misl. As the Ramgharias also returned from the vanguard, So did the scheduled caste Singhs Misl in a body. (28)
lines: As S.
Hari Singh Bhangi returned with his contingent,
So did S.
Hari Singh, the chief of the Nankai Misl.
As the Ramgharias also returned from the vanguard,
So did the scheduled caste Singhs Misl in a body.

blocks.text: Hearing the drum beat, the Ghanaiyas also turned back, So did the Singhpuria join this expedition. They were joined by the Singhs' from Dalewalia Misl, Who were on very friendly terms with S. Tara Singh. (29)
lines: Hearing the drum beat, the Ghanaiyas also turned back,
So did the Singhpuria join this expedition.
They were joined by the Singhs' from Dalewalia Misl,
Who were on very friendly terms with S.
Tara Singh.

blocks.text: The young Singhs belonging to Sodhi, Bedi and Shaheed Misls, They also joined along with Singhs of Amritsari Misl. As the Khalsa flag bearers unfurled their flags, The Singhs from the Shukarchakia Misl also raised war slogans. (30)
lines: The young Singhs belonging to Sodhi,
Bedi and Shaheed Misls,
They also joined along with Singhs of Amritsari Misl.
As the Khalsa flag bearers unfurled their flags,
The Singhs from the Shukarchakia Misl also raised war slogans.

blocks.text: Dohra:

These Muslim Ranghars of Morinda were the real culprits, Who had handed over the Guru's Sahibzadas to (Wazir Khan), Identifying all these culprits responsible for that act, The Khalsa Panth attacked Morinda from all the sides. (31)
lines: These Muslim Ranghars of Morinda were the real culprits,
Who had handed over the Guru's Sahibzadas to (Wazir Khan),
Identifying all these culprits responsible for that act,
The Khalsa Panth attacked Morinda from all the sides.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As water creates a gurgling sound when it goes down stream, As a ship sinks in the ocean when water enters its inside, So did the Singhs keep pouring into Morinda while fighting, Killing everyone whosoever came across their way. (32)
lines: As water creates a gurgling sound when it goes down stream,
As a ship sinks in the ocean when water enters its inside,
So did the Singhs keep pouring into Morinda while fighting,
Killing everyone whosoever came across their way.

blocks.text: The defiant Muslim Ranghars entered into a formidable fort, Which had steep walls surrounded by a water channel. As they went into the fort after shutting its big doors, Nobody could climb up the fort's steep high walls. (33)
lines: The defiant Muslim Ranghars entered into a formidable fort,
Which had steep walls surrounded by a water channel.
As they went into the fort after shutting its big doors,
Nobody could climb up the fort's steep high walls.

blocks.text: Being protected by a deep channel and high walled fort, The (defiant) Ranghars felt very proud of their safety. While no Singh could come out who fell into that channel, Very steep high walls did the Singhs find on the other side. (34)
lines: Being protected by a deep channel and high walled fort,
The (defiant) Ranghars felt very proud of their safety.
While no Singh could come out who fell into that channel,
Very steep high walls did the Singhs find on the other side.

blocks.text: Then did the Khalsa chiefs made an observation, That Sirhind town was only nine miles from Morinda. Lest the Pathan reinforcements might launch an attack, The Khalsa must guard against such an eventuality. (35)
lines: Then did the Khalsa chiefs made an observation,
That Sirhind town was only nine miles from Morinda.
Lest the Pathan reinforcements might launch an attack,
The Khalsa must guard against such an eventuality.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Then did S. Charat Singh make a bold declaration, He must be allowed to take care of that side. The Khalsa Panth must not worry about the Pathans, They must attempt to get the closed doors open. (36)
lines: Then did S.
Charat Singh make a bold declaration,
He must be allowed to take care of that side.
The Khalsa Panth must not worry about the Pathans,
They must attempt to get the closed doors open.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Once again did S. Charat Singh repeat his declaration, Definitely would he be responsible for guarding Sirhind side. Declaring this, as S. Charat Singh proceeded towards Sirhind, The Gilja Pathans felt scared of the Singhs' advance. (37)
lines: Once again did S.
Charat Singh repeat his declaration,
Definitely would he be responsible for guarding Sirhind side.
Declaring this, as S.
Charat Singh proceeded towards Sirhind,
The Gilja Pathans felt scared of the Singhs' advance.

blocks.text: There arose a lot of din and noise from the outside, As a lot of scarce has spread on both the sides. Now listen to the account of the other side, As Khalsa Panth decided to slaughter all the Muslims. (38)
lines: There arose a lot of din and noise from the outside,
As a lot of scarce has spread on both the sides.
Now listen to the account of the other side,
As Khalsa Panth decided to slaughter all the Muslims.

blocks.text: They must spare those who have tufts of hair on their heads, All the other inhabitants must the Khalsa slaughter. After making a congregational prayer to this effect, Khalsa Panth started beating war drums on all the sides. (39)
lines: They must spare those who have tufts of hair on their heads,
All the other inhabitants must the Khalsa slaughter.
After making a congregational prayer to this effect,
Khalsa Panth started beating war drums on all the sides.

blocks.text: As the Singhs felt excited at the beat of wardrums, They did not spare any enemy of the Khalsa Panth. As the Khalsa force launched an attack from all sides, The din and dust created a pall of darkness all around. (40)
lines: As the Singhs felt excited at the beat of wardrums,
They did not spare any enemy of the Khalsa Panth.
As the Khalsa force launched an attack from all sides,
The din and dust created a pall of darkness all around.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Such an attack did the Singhs launch on the fort, As had the Monkey army (or Hanuman) made on Sri Lanka. They were the first to climb up the steep walls, Who had arrived from the farthest end. (41)
lines: Such an attack did the Singhs launch on the fort,
As had the Monkey army (or Hanuman) made on Sri Lanka.
They were the first to climb up the steep walls,
Who had arrived from the farthest end.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Singhs opened a volley of fire after their arrival, They did not know whether it hit anybody or not. As the Singhs fired shots from a close range, The Ranghars kept on dying as it hit their heads. (42)
lines: As the Singhs opened a volley of fire after their arrival,
They did not know whether it hit anybody or not.
As the Singhs fired shots from a close range,
The Ranghars kept on dying as it hit their heads.

blocks.text: As the deep channel now appeared to be very shallow, So did the steep walls appear to be so small. As an each Singh picked up another to make a step-ladder, The Singhs kept climbing up without any ladders. (43)
lines: As the deep channel now appeared to be very shallow,
So did the steep walls appear to be so small.
As an each Singh picked up another to make a step-ladder,
The Singhs kept climbing up without any ladders.

blocks.text: As the Singhs wielded their swords on climbing up, Many a Ranghar did they slaughter and kill. As the Gharuan Singhs entered the blacksmiths' houses, Sledge hammers did the Singhs pick up from there. (44)
lines: As the Singhs wielded their swords on climbing up,
Many a Ranghar did they slaughter and kill.
As the Gharuan Singhs entered the blacksmiths' houses,
Sledge hammers did the Singhs pick up from there.

blocks.text: Many a Ranghars' heads did they crush with hammers, As they struck the Ranghars with all their might. Being familiar with the faces of (wicked) Ranghars, They killed those culprits who were their chiefs. (45)
lines: Many a Ranghars' heads did they crush with hammers,
As they struck the Ranghars with all their might.
Being familiar with the faces of (wicked) Ranghars,
They killed those culprits who were their chiefs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Jaani Khan and Maani Khan4 were their names, Who were the chief officials among the Ranghars. These two were the main culprits (in the town of Morinda), Who had handed over the Sahibzadas (to Wazir Khan). (46)
lines: Jaani Khan and Maani Khan4 were their names,
Who were the chief officials among the Ranghars.
These two were the main culprits (in the town of Morinda),
Who had handed over the Sahibzadas (to Wazir Khan).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs from Gharuan took out those culprits, Their sons did the Singhs first crush with hammers. Thereafter, the Singhs identified their grandsons, The whole of their progeny did the Singhs eliminate. (47)
lines: The Singhs from Gharuan took out those culprits,
Their sons did the Singhs first crush with hammers.
Thereafter, the Singhs identified their grandsons,
The whole of their progeny did the Singhs eliminate.

blocks.text: As Guru's progeny had been slaughtered by these Ranghars, How could the Ranghars own progeny survive (after this sin)? As the Guru had heard about the execution of the Sahibzadas, He had learnt about the role of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan. (48)
lines: As Guru's progeny had been slaughtered by these Ranghars,
How could the Ranghars own progeny survive (after this sin)?
As the Guru had heard about the execution of the Sahibzadas,
He had learnt about the role of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan.

blocks.text: The revered Guru had then let out such a curse, That the whole progeny of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan would be uprooted. So was their whole progeny eliminated till the last survivor, As the Guru's prophetic curse had uprooted their dynasty. (49)
lines: The revered Guru had then let out such a curse,
That the whole progeny of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan would be uprooted.
So was their whole progeny eliminated till the last survivor,
As the Guru's prophetic curse had uprooted their dynasty.

blocks.text: The remaining Ranghar chiefs related to these two culprits, They, too, were done to death with the blows of hammers. None of the Singhs indulged in looting and plundering the city, As all of them rushed to slaughter the Ranghars first. (50)
lines: The remaining Ranghar chiefs related to these two culprits,
They, too, were done to death with the blows of hammers.
None of the Singhs indulged in looting and plundering the city,
As all of them rushed to slaughter the Ranghars first.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Singhs, being extremely outraged (at the execution of Sahibzadas), Their swords did they wield in such a rage. Sparing all those having tufts of hair on their heads, The Singhs slaughtered all other inhabitants of the town. (51)
lines: The Singhs, being extremely outraged (at the execution of Sahibzadas),
Their swords did they wield in such a rage.
Sparing all those having tufts of hair on their heads,
The Singhs slaughtered all other inhabitants of the town.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whichever Muslim Ranghar took refuge in a Hindu household, Their progeny survived this (ruthless) massacre by Singhs. Why get the innocent Sahibzadas arrested in vain, So had said some of the relations of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan? (52)
lines: Whichever Muslim Ranghar took refuge in a Hindu household,
Their progeny survived this (ruthless) massacre by Singhs.
Why get the innocent Sahibzadas arrested in vain,
So had said some of the relations of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan?

blocks.text: They had advised the Ranghar chiefs against committing that crime, But their advice had Jaani Khan and Maani Khan turned down. Their plea for mercy was instrumental in saving their progeny, As they had pleaded like the Malkekotla chiefs. (53)
lines: They had advised the Ranghar chiefs against committing that crime,
But their advice had Jaani Khan and Maani Khan turned down.
Their plea for mercy was instrumental in saving their progeny,
As they had pleaded like the Malkekotla chiefs.

blocks.text: As darkness descended in the midst of loot and slaughter, Many a Ranghar survive under the cover of darkness. Those who had taken refuge in the Hindu households, They were turned out at night to save their lives. (54)
lines: As darkness descended in the midst of loot and slaughter,
Many a Ranghar survive under the cover of darkness.
Those who had taken refuge in the Hindu households,
They were turned out at night to save their lives.

blocks.text: Jaani Khan and Maani Khan were these two brothers, They had got the (two younger) Sahibzadas arrested. After this had the revered Guru thus remarked: Never would Jaani Khan and Maani Khan survive. (55)
lines: Jaani Khan and Maani Khan were these two brothers,
They had got the (two younger) Sahibzadas arrested.
After this had the revered Guru thus remarked: Never would Jaani Khan and Maani Khan survive.

blocks.text: Dohra:
After the massacre and occupation of Morinda, Highly delighted did the Khalsa Panth Singhs feel. Highly helpless did the Durrani forces feel, Extremely rewarded did the Khalsa Singhs feel. (56)
lines: After the massacre and occupation of Morinda,
Highly delighted did the Khalsa Panth Singhs feel.
Highly helpless did the Durrani forces feel,
Extremely rewarded did the Khalsa Singhs feel.

blocks.text: The account that had the author (Rattan Singh) heard, So much had he narrated (about this incident). Whatever further events had the author heard about, So should the enlightened readers lend their ears to. (57)
lines: The account that had the author (Rattan Singh) heard,
So much had he narrated (about this incident).
Whatever further events had the author heard about,
So should the enlightened readers lend their ears to.
